description: We are MeteoriteEaters, a passionate tech team participating in the Haldwani local event for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. We specialize in software development, full-stack web engineering, and data-driven solutions. For this hackathon, we are tackling real-world challenges using open NASA data to build innovative tools. We are looking for collaborative developers, designers, and data enthusiasts to join our team!
summary: We built FieldWise, a practical web app that helps Indian farmers plan smarter, climate-resilient 3-season crop rotations. Instead of guessing what to plant next, a farmer simply enters their district, soil type, irrigation level, and farm size. Behind the scenes, FieldWise pulls live NASA POWER satellite data—tracking temperature, rainfall, and surface soil wetness—and pairs it with Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) guidelines to recommend full annual crop cycles tailored to their land.   This directly tackles the Field Shift challenge by turning raw space-based weather and soil moisture telemetry into clear, everyday planting decisions. Farmers can compare top rotation options, spot rainfall risks early, and see the nitrogen and pest-break benefits scaled to their exact acreage.   For smallholder farmers, erratic monsoons and continuous monocropping quietly drain soil health and harvests. Because ground sensors are too expensive for most villages, FieldWise relies on open NASA satellite data, works in both English and Hindi, and lets farmers download an offline farm plan to carry straight to their local agriculture center.
details: What It Does & How It WorksFieldWise (AGRO-SAT) is an interactive web application that helps Indian farmers plan climate-resilient, 3-season crop rotations using live satellite telemetry. Rather than guessing what to sow next, a farmer simply selects their state, enters their district or city (such as Haldwani or Panjim), and fills in basic field details—soil type, irrigation availability, farm area in hectares, current crop, and primary farming goal. Behind the scenes, FieldWise converts that location into exact latitude and longitude coordinates, pins the active agricultural sector on a map, and queries the open NASA POWER Agroclimatology (AG) API. It pulls four key Earth-observation metrics: Surface Air Temperature (T2M): Checks thermal compatibility across Kharif, Rabi, and Zaid growing windows. Bias-Corrected Precipitation (PRECTOTCORR): Tracks monthly rainfall baselines and calculates rainfall variability risk using the Coefficient of Variation (CV). Surface Soil Wetness (GWETTOP): Measures top-layer soil moisture so crop water demand matches actual field conditions. All-Sky Surface Solar Irradiance (ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN): Evaluates available solar energy for photosynthesis and crop growth.Our scoring engine combines these NASA climate baselines with Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) agronomy guidelines to rank full annual rotation sequences (for example, Wheat → Mung Bean → Sorghum). Farmers can compare the top four rotation pathways side by side, explore monthly climate charts, search an All-India crop matrix, and download an offline advisory report. Key BenefitsZero Field-Hardware Cost: Replaces expensive on-farm weather and soil sensors with open, globally gridded NASA satellite data backed by MERRA-2 and CERES reanalysis. Smarter Water & Fertilizer Management: Matches low- or high-water crops to real soil moisture and irrigation limits while prioritizing legume rotations that naturally fix atmospheric nitrogen. One-Click Bilingual Accessibility: Switches seamlessly between English and Hindi (हिन्दी), translating every chart, crop sequence, and risk explanation into clear, farmer-friendly language. Offline Field Readiness: Exports a clean .txt farm plan that farmers can save on their phones or carry to local Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) extension centers without needing active internet. Intended ImpactContinuous monocropping and unpredictable monsoons slowly strip soil of nitrogen, lock in soil-borne diseases, and put smallholder livelihoods at risk. FieldWise is built to bridge the gap between space-agency science and everyday village farming. By guiding farmers toward diversified, multi-family crop cycles, the platform aims to cut down synthetic urea dependency, conserve groundwater, naturally break recurring pest cycles, and help rural farms adapt to shifting local climates. Tools, Languages, Software & Hardware UsedProgramming Language: Python 3. Web Framework & Interface: Streamlit, styled with custom CSS, responsive HTML cards, and custom SVG iconography (components/ui_cards.py). Data & Visualization Libraries: Pandas for time-series aggregation and rotation scoring, Plotly (graph_objects and make_subplots) for interactive dual-axis climate charts and suitability bar rankings, and st.map for spatial sector mapping. APIs & Scientific Data: NASA Langley Research Center’s NASA POWER API, geocoding endpoints via Python requests, and ICAR crop rotation manuals. Development Environment & Hardware: Visual Studio Code, Git, GitHub, and standard consumer laptops for development, testing, and deployment. How Our Project Is CreativeFull 3-Season Biological Sequencing: Instead of predicting a single isolated crop, FieldWise maps a complete 12-month journey (Phase 1 Baseline → Phase 2 Climate & Family Shift → Phase 3 Soil Recovery Bridge), rewarding sequences that rotate across distinct plant families (such as Poaceae to Fabaceae). Dynamic Hectare Impact Calculator: Translates abstract agronomic metrics into tangible, farm-scale outcomes—calculating estimated nitrogen offset and multi-family pest-break benefits scaled directly to the user’s acreage. Honest "96% Realism Cap": Rather than presenting overly confident 100% scores, we intentionally capped suitability ratings at 96% and highlighted rainfall volatility (CV) alongside KVK advisory reminders so farmers treat the tool as transparent decision support. Factors Our Team ConsideredRural Connectivity & Language Barriers: Knowing that internet access in fields can be unreliable and technical English can alienate growers, we prioritized fast loading, a clean visual layout, full Hindi localization, and offline .txt report downloads. Local Soil & Irrigation Realities: A crop suited to loamy, irrigated land can fail in sandy, rain-fed plots. Every pathway weighs soil texture, irrigation supply, and satellite surface wetness together before scoring. Scientific Transparency & Trust: Farmers and agricultural advisors need to know why a rotation is recommended, so every pathway displays exact NASA temperature and soil moisture evidence alongside trade-off warnings and ICAR citations.
